statement: Which of these gives an odd answer?

choices.misconception: I thought odd plus odd gives an odd number, but two odd numbers always add to an even number.
I thought an odd number times an even number stays odd, but multiplying by an even number always gives an even answer.
I mixed up the rule and thought an even number minus an even number could be odd.
I looked only at the first number, 11, which is odd, and ignored the even 12.

hints: Look at whether each number is odd or even, not at its size.
Odd and even follow fixed rules for adding, taking away and multiplying. Decide each one from the last digits alone.
Odd + odd is even, even + odd is odd, and any multiplication with an even number in it is even.

solutions.reliable: Work each one out: 18 + 31 = 49, 15 + 27 = 42, 23 x 4 = 92, 36 - 14 = 22 and 11 x 12 = 132. Only 49 is odd. The transferable idea: when unsure, a quick full calculation settles it, but the last digit is all that decides odd or even.
solutions.elegant: Use the rules: odd + odd is even, even - even is even, and a product with an even number in it is even. Only 18 + 31 adds one even and one odd number, so it is the only odd answer. The transferable idea: odd or even can be decided without the full answer.

whyOnTest: The odd and even rules for sums and products let you answer without calculating, which is what this probes.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
